entries.content:
Vercel and ElevenLabs are partnering to bring 14 ElevenLabs models to AI Gateway. To celebrate the launch, all ElevenLabs models are 50% off on AI Gateway for the first 14 days, through November 9th.

AI Gateway supports six different types of ElevenLabs audio models:

  • Speech to text: Transcribe recordings or caption live audio as people speak.

  • Streaming text to speech: Start playing audio while a language model is still writing its reply, so users don't have to wait for the full answer.

  • Realtime voice agents: Let users talk to your app and listen to it respond out loud in a single live session. Useful for support lines, tutors, and in-app assistants.

  • Music: Describe a track in plain text and get back a finished song or instrumental at the length you need.

  • Sound effects: Generate game and interface sounds, or ambience that loops cleanly, from a short description.

  • Multi-voice dialogue: Voice a whole conversation in one call, with a different voice for each speaker.

All of these audio models are accessible through a single gateway API key. Your app or agent can transcribe what a user says, reason over it with your choice of hundreds of models, then answer in an ElevenLabs voice. You can also create soundtracks with generated music and sound effects.

Every request lands in the same usage, cost, and trace views as your other AI Gateway traffic.

Copy link to headingModel types

AI Gateway gives you access to 14 ElevenLabs models, spanning speech to text, realtime voice, and music.

Copy link to headingSpeech and transcription

Scribe v2 Realtime turns a user's speech into text while they are still talking. A language model of your choice then writes the answer. Eleven Flash v2.5, a low-latency ElevenLabs voice model, reads that answer aloud as it streams in, so the user hears the reply begin before the model finishes writing it.

Because each step is its own model, you can swap the transcription, language, or speech model without touching the rest of the pipeline.

In the example below, a user asks whether they’ll make a connecting flight. The text model combines flight status and gate distance to answer, then the speech model delivers the response.

      
import {  experimental_streamSpeech as streamSpeech,  experimental_streamTranscribe as streamTranscribe,  streamText,} from 'ai';
const heard = streamTranscribe({  model: 'elevenlabs/scribe-v2-realtime',  audio: microphoneStream,  inputAudioFormat: { type: 'audio/pcm', rate: 16000 },});
const { textStream } = streamText({  model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5',  prompt: await heard.text,});
const { audioStream } = streamSpeech({  model: 'elevenlabs/eleven-flash-v2.5',  text: textStream,  voice: 'hpp4J3VqNfWAUOO0d1Us',});

The code transcribes a 16 kHz microphone stream, sends the finished transcript to a language model, and pipes the model’s text straight into speech.

Copy link to headingRealtime voice agents

Eleven Realtime v1 Max and Eleven Realtime v1 Mini run the whole spoken conversation in one model, which suits conversations where users expect natural back-and-forth, like a support call or an in-app assistant. Both models take the user's audio in and speak a reply back over a single WebSocket session, so there's no separate transcription or speech step to wire up.

Eleven Realtime hears “Can I change the delivery address for my order?” and responds “I can help with that. What’s your order number?” over one WebSocket session.

      
import { gateway } from 'ai';
const { token, url } = await gateway.experimental_realtime.getToken({  model: 'elevenlabs/eleven-realtime-v1-max',});

The browser opens the WebSocket session itself, so the server’s only job is to mint a short-lived token for your chosen model, which keeps your API key off the client.

In the browser, connect with the 

useRealtime
hook from 
@ai-sdk/react
, which handles the WebSocket connection, microphone capture, and audio playback. In the hook's 
sessionConfig
, set an ElevenLabs voice ID and 
turnDetection: { type: 'semantic-vad' }
. These models support semantic voice activity detection (VAD) to decide when the user has finished speaking, but they don't support 
server-vad
. The realtime guide walks through the full browser setup.

Copy link to headingMusic and sound effects

Music v2.5 and Music v2 compose original music from a text description. Name a genre, a mood, or the instruments you want, and the model returns a finished track at the length you ask for, with or without vocals. For more control, you can lay out a song section by section and give each section its own style and length.

Sound Effects v2 works the same way for shorter sounds, such as footsteps, a door slamming, or rain that loops under a game level.

All three models use 

generateSpeech
, with 
text
describing the sound you want instead of words to read aloud. This example requests a 30-second track: 
      
import { generateSpeech } from 'ai';
const { audio } = await generateSpeech({  model: 'elevenlabs/music-v2.5',  text: 'A mellow lo-fi beat with soft piano',  providerOptions: { elevenlabs: { musicLengthMs: 30000 } },});

Copy link to headingMulti-voice dialogue

Eleven v4, Eleven v4 Turbo, and Eleven v3 perform a script with several speakers in a single request. You assign a voice to each line, and each change of voice starts a new turn. A two-host podcast or a scene with a full cast comes back as one continuous recording, so there are no separate clips to stitch together.

      
import { experimental_streamSpeech as streamSpeech } from 'ai';
const host = 'hpp4J3VqNfWAUOO0d1Us';const guest = 'CwhRBWXzGAHq8TQ4Fs17';
const { audioStream } = streamSpeech({  model: 'elevenlabs/eleven-v4',  text: [    { type: 'text', text: 'Did the deploy go out?', voice: host },    { type: 'text', text: 'It shipped an hour ago.', voice: guest },  ],  providerOptions: { elevenlabs: { dialogue: { voices: [host, guest] } } },});

Each voice is an ElevenLabs voice ID. Parts can also stream in from a language model writing the script.

Copy link to headingAbout AI Gateway

AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more.

AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and doesn't charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.

The AI Gateway audio docs have examples across the ElevenLabs models. Browse all audio models on AI Gateway, and try ElevenLabs at 50% off until November 9th.

entries.title: AI traffic insights now available in Vercel Observability
entries.summary: You can now query AI traffic in Vercel Observability to understand how AI bots are accessing your site.AI traffic insights show:Requests by verified AI bot: how many requests each bot makesMost-crawled pages: pages most frequently requested by AI crawlers for indexing or model trainingAssistant retrievals: pages AI assistants fetch in response to user actions or search queriesMarkdown requests: pa
entries.content:
You can now query AI traffic in Vercel Observability to understand how AI bots are accessing your site.

AI traffic insights show:

  • Requests by verified AI bot: how many requests each bot makes

  • Most-crawled pages: pages most frequently requested by AI crawlers for indexing or model training

  • Assistant retrievals: pages AI assistants fetch in response to user actions or search queries

  • Markdown requests: pages AI bots request in Markdown format

  • Errors: pages where requests from AI bots return errors

To view AI traffic insights, open Observability > AI Traffic in the Vercel dashboard.

You and your agents can also query these metrics with 

vercel metrics
in the Vercel CLI. CLI queries require Observability Plus. 
      
vc metrics vercel.ai_traffic.count --group-by botName

AI traffic to your site broken down by bot name

Learn more in the AI traffic documentation.

entries.title: Vercel Agent sessions now cost 67% less
entries.summary: Vercel Agent sessions in the dashboard and Slack now cost 67% less on average. We rebuilt how Agent manages context, reducing the tokens needed per session and improving prompt-cache reuse. These improvements are live and require no action. What changed: Workflow-based CLI skills: Updated Vercel CLI skills give agents clearer guidance for common workflows and error recovery. Other agents using the
entries.content:
Vercel Agent sessions in the dashboard and Slack now cost 67% less on average. We rebuilt how Agent manages context, reducing the tokens needed per session and improving prompt-cache reuse. These improvements are live and require no action.

What changed:

  • Workflow-based CLI skills: Updated Vercel CLI skills give agents clearer guidance for common workflows and error recovery. Other agents using these skills also benefit.

  • Incremental context management: Agent manages context more efficiently as conversations grow, including long Slack threads.

  • Improved prompt caching: Agent preserves more reusable context across turns so more of it can be read from the cache.

  • More efficient coding and planning: Updated guidance helps Agent plan changes and write code with fewer tokens.

Vercel Agent’s billing rates are unchanged. Paid sessions are billed at the model provider’s inference rates plus a Vercel Agent fee of $0.25 per million tokens. View usage and costs in the Agent section of your dashboard.

entries.title: HarnessAgent now supports image inputs for all harness adapters
entries.summary: The AI SDK HarnessAgent layer now accepts image inputs across every harness adapter.Pass images alongside text in the standard AI SDK message format: a content array mixing { type: 'text' } and { type: 'file' } parts.Image input is processed by the harnesses' underlying vision models and supported across all available adapters: Claude Code, Cline, Codex, Cursor, Deep Agents, fx, GitHub Copilot, Gr
entries.content:
The AI SDK 

HarnessAgent
layer now accepts image inputs across every harness adapter.

Pass images alongside text in the standard AI SDK message format: a 

content
array mixing 
{ type: 'text' }
and 
{ type: 'file' }
parts.

Image input is processed by the harnesses' underlying vision models and supported across all available adapters: Claude Code, Cline, Codex, Cursor, Deep Agents, fx, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, OpenCode, Pi.

      
import { HarnessAgent } from '@ai-sdk/harness/agent';import { codex } from '@ai-sdk/harness-codex';import { createVercelNetworkSandboxSession } from '@ai-sdk/sandbox-vercel';import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
const agent = new HarnessAgent({ harness: codex });
const sandboxSession = await createVercelNetworkSandboxSession({  runtime: 'node24',  ports: [4000],  template: await agent.getSandboxTemplate(),});const session = await agent.createSession({ sandboxSession });
const result = await agent.generate({  session,  messages: [    {      role: 'user',      content: [        { type: 'text', text: 'Describe the image in one sentence.' },        {          type: 'file',          mediaType: 'image/png',          data: readFileSync('image.png'),        },      ],    },  ],});

Basic example asking the Codex harness to describe a given image

Read the 

HarnessAgent
image inputs documentation to get started.

entries.content:
You and your agents can now browse and search more than 1000 services available in Vercel Connect without leaving your terminal. 

vercel connect discover
searches by name, alias, keyword, and description. 
      
vercel connect discover crm

Results can be filtered by category, connection method (such as 

mcp
or 
oauth
) or the product a service exposes. You can also limit results to services that forward webhook triggers. 
vercel connect categories
lists the category slugs you can filter by. Both commands support 
--format=json
for scripts and agents. 
      
vercel connect discover --category ai --category datavercel connect discover --connection-method mcpvercel connect discover --supports-triggers

You can then pass the service name while creating any connector to the command:

      
vercel connect create slack

Create a slack connector via CLI.

Update to version 64.1.0 or later of the CLI to get started, and read the Vercel Connect CLI docs to learn more.

entries.content:
AgentEnv, Scale AI's framework for testing agents against tasks and scoring their results, now runs on Vercel Sandbox. The Vercel provider ships in AgentEnv 0.9.1334 and later, and runs the agent and its task environment in separate Sandboxes.

Try the AgentEnv example to run an evaluation on Vercel Sandbox and inspect the task’s score and the agent’s recorded actions. After completing the setup guide, run this command from the cloned repository. It uses your existing Vercel CLI login:

      
./vercel-eval --scope YOUR_TEAM --project YOUR_PROJECT

Replace 

YOUR_TEAM
with your Vercel team slug and 
YOUR_PROJECT
with an existing project name.

Learn more in the Sandbox ecosystem documentation.

entries.summary: You can now create custom monitors to get alerts based on your Vercel Observability query results. For example, you can track signals such as AI Gateway costs, Core Web Vitals and other performance metrics, Workflow and external API failure rates, or Vercel Sandbox CPU time.Each monitor tracks a single metric, such as response time, or a ratio of two metrics, such as errors divided by total reques
entries.content:
You can now create custom monitors to get alerts based on your Vercel Observability query results.

For example, you can track signals such as AI Gateway costs, Core Web Vitals and other performance metrics, Workflow and external API failure rates, or Vercel Sandbox CPU time.

Each monitor tracks a single metric, such as response time, or a ratio of two metrics, such as errors divided by total requests. Choose statistical anomaly detection or a fixed threshold, then configure the detection window, filters, and grouping.

To create a monitor, inspect a chart’s query in Observability, start from a preset, or open Settings > Alerts for your team.

You can also define a custom monitor in a JSON file and create it with 

vercel monitors add
in the Vercel CLI. Run 
vercel monitors schema --type custom
for the schema and examples.

Receive alerts through email, Slack, Vercel Inbox, push notifications, or team-level webhooks. You can also add context for Vercel Agent to use when investigating an alert.

Custom monitors are available on Pro and Enterprise plans with Observability Plus, at $0.0035 per GB of data scanned. Built-in alerts remain included with Observability Plus.

Create a custom monitor or learn more in the configuration documentation.

entries.content:
Vercel Agent can now investigate alerts from Vercel monitors before they reach your paging system. With validation enabled for a webhook destination, only alerts Agent classifies as Critical are sent to it.

To enable validation:

  • Open a monitor’s notification settings and create or link a webhook destination for your paging system, such as incident.io.

  • Select Critical Only next to that destination.

You can also configure notification destinations with the Vercel CLI using 

vercel monitors notifications
. Add 
--critical-only
when linking or updating a webhook destination.

Agent checks logs and metrics to assess impact. For example, it can identify health-check errors that don’t affect customers or confirm sustained 5xx errors affecting checkout requests. You can also add context to each monitor to guide Agent’s investigation.

Alert validation is available on Pro and Enterprise plans with Observability Plus. Observability Plus includes 10 Agent investigations per billing cycle, with additional investigations billed separately. Custom monitors cost $0.0035 per GB of data scanned. Built-in alerts remain included with Observability Plus.

Learn more in the alert webhook documentation.

entries.content:
Vercel Sandbox now lets you send input to running commands through standard input (stdin). Use it to exchange messages with stdio MCP servers such as agent-browser, or send data to other command-line programs while they run.

In the TypeScript SDK, set 

stdin: true
and 
detached: true
in 
runCommand()
. Use 
writeStdin()
to send input and 
closeStdin()
when you’re done: 
      
import { Sandbox } from '@vercel/sandbox';
const sandbox = await Sandbox.create();const cmd = await sandbox.runCommand({  cmd: 'cat',  stdin: true,  detached: true,});
await cmd.writeStdin('hello');await cmd.closeStdin();
const result = await cmd.wait();console.log(await result.stdout()); // "hello"

Send input to a running command and read its output with the Sandbox TypeScript SDK.

You can also set 

stdin
to a Node.js readable stream, such as 
process.stdin
. The SDK forwards the stream’s data and closes the command’s standard input when the stream ends.

In the Python SDK, set 

stdin=subprocess.PIPE
and send input with 
server.stdin.send()
. Call 
communicate()
to close stdin, collect remaining output, and wait for the process to exit: 
      
import subprocess
from vercel import sandboxfrom vercel.api import session
async with session():    async with sandbox.create_sandbox() as instance:        server = await instance.create_process("cat", stdin=subprocess.PIPE)        await server.stdin.send(b"ping\n")        print(await server.stdout.readline())        print(await server.communicate())

Write to a running process’s stdin and read its output with the Sandbox Python SDK.

For commands that receive all their input at once, you can pass 

input
directly to Python’s 
run_process()
.

Read the Sandbox documentation to get started.

entries.content:
The Overview tab in the dashboard now lets you choose which metric appears on each project card.

Project cards used to show a fixed Real Experience Score in the top right, but not everyone on your team watches the same signal. You can now swap that slot for whichever metric matters for that project. A security-sensitive project can show firewall activity, while a marketing site project shows traffic.

Copy link to headingAvailable widgets

  • Firewall: allowed requests, denied requests

  • Observability: alerts, edge requests, function invocations, error rate

  • Speed Insights: Real Experience Score, LCP, CLS

  • Web Analytics: visitors online, visitors, page views

Copy link to headingPick per project

Open the switcher in the top right of any project card. The menu shows the current value for each available metric. When you select one, your choice is saved for that project and follows your account across refreshes and devices.

Copy link to headingEnable features from the card

If a project does not have a feature enabled, you can start the enable flow from the widget menu without leaving the Overview tab. This is available for Speed Insights Plus, Web Analytics, and alerts.

Copy link to headingGet started

Open your team’s Overview tab and use the switcher on any project card.
